caption:
Glass skin is the English name that travelled. The Korean word it came from, 물광 (mul-gwang), means something closer to water-shine: light sitting just under skin that is holding water.

The difference matters more than it sounds. Glass skin describes a surface you can photograph. 물광 describes a state the skin is in. One is about how it looks; the other is about what it is doing.

The same gap shows up elsewhere. Dehydrated is not quite 속당김 (sok-dang-gim), an inner pull - skin that can be oily on top and tight underneath. Texture is not quite 결 (gyeol), which is closer to the grain of the skin.

This is a language note, not a clinical claim.

General education only.
